name: binsearch
axis: binary search over a large sorted array — latency-bound unpredictable access plus one data-dependent branch per probe
n: N=4000000 sorted i32 (16MB), QUERIES=6000000 (~22 probes each, ~132M probes)
nPython: N=4000000, QUERIES=300000 (20x fewer queries; multiply Python's wall time by 20 to compare)
notes: Hand-written, NOT slice::binary_search / bisect: all four run the same loop. The array holds 0,3,6,... and keys are drawn from a MINSTD stream over [0,3N), so about one query in three hits. Output is two lines: the hit count and the sum of found indices (3.99e12, exact in i64 and in a JS Number). The search loop terminates by setting lo = hi + 1 rather than returning early, identically in all four. Setup (4M pushes) is ~4% of the VL time at these sizes. Scale-verified by doubling QUERIES: vl 2.28x, rs 2.22x, js 2.01x, py 1.93x.
